The test image shows a tomato leaf with large, irregular brown/tan necrotic lesions covering much of the leaf, with surrounding yellow/chlorotic tissue. No powdery coating, no target rings. This pattern suggests Late Blight, Phytophthora Blight, or possibly Leaf Mold as top candidates.

Let me view one reference from each of 8 different classes to compare.
Late Blight reference is very similar to the test image — large brown necrosis on leaf placed on a flat surface. Let me check more classes.
Phytophthora Blight shows stem lesions — doesn't match the test image leaf pattern. Let me check Leaf Mold and Early Blight.
Early Blight shows target rings - doesn't match the large continuous necrosis in the test. Let me check Septoria and Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus.

All 8 reference images viewed from 8 different classes. Here's my analysis:

**Test image features:** Single tomato leaf on white background, large irregular brown/tan necrotic lesion covering most of the leaf, with yellow/chlorotic tissue surrounding the necrosis. No visible concentric rings, no powdery coating, no small scattered spots.

**Comparison results:**
- **Late_Blight** (CDDM_498.jpg): Extremely close match — same presentation of a detached leaf on flat surface with large continuous brown necrosis covering the majority of the leaf, remaining green tissue at edges. Best visual match.
- **Phytophthora_Blight**: Stem cankers on whole plant — no match.
- **Leaf_Mold**: Pale yellow-green patches — no match.
- **Early_Blight**: Target/concentric ring spots — no match.
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: Small scattered dark spots — no match.
- **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus**: Whole plant wilting — no match.
- **Gray_Mold**: Fruit infection with gray fungal growth — no match.
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato**: Marginal edge necrosis on attached leaves — partial similarity but different distribution pattern.

Late Blight is the clear winner based on visual similarity — the large, spreading irregular brown necrosis on a detached leaf matches the reference almost exactly.
